relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - applied against the whole enum (both Basic and Advanced) rather than one specific value, since the statement text names cluster access credentials generically, not one credential type
relations.evidence: You cannot execute this statement using [cluster access credentials](../../clusters/cluster-rbac.md).

notable_absence.finding: No credential-type-keyed privilege pair (Basic/Advanced) at all for this statement - it sits entirely in the management-plane capella-role track and is explicitly excluded from the data-plane credential-type track. Confirms the hypothesis that a DDL statement belongs to one access-control track or the other, not both.

cross_component_finding: Strong confirmation that the two-track Capella access-control model (management-plane capella-role gate vs. data-plane credential-type privilege pair) generalizes cleanly to bucket-level DDL: ALTER BUCKET is purely management-plane-gated and explicitly forbidden from data-plane credentials, contrasting directly with ALTER SEQUENCE in this same batch, which is purely data-plane-gated via the Basic/Advanced privilege pair and names no capella-role at all.
